blocks.title: Constant acceleration
blocks.md: With initial velocity $u$, final velocity $v$, acceleration $a$, time $t$, displacement $s$: $v=u+at$; $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2$; $v^2=u^2+2as$; $s=\frac{(u+v)}{2}t$. Units: m, m/s, m/s², s. Falling or thrown objects: $a=g=10$ m/s² (we use 10; some books use 9.8).

blocks.title: Graphs
blocks.md: On a velocity–time graph the **gradient** is the acceleration and the **area** under the graph is the distance travelled (displacement if signed). On a displacement–time graph the gradient is the velocity.

blocks.title: Calculus link
blocks.md: For variable acceleration: velocity $v=\frac{ds}{dt}$ and acceleration $a=\frac{dv}{dt}=\frac{d^2s}{dt^2}$. Conversely $v=\int a\,dt$ and $s=\int v\,dt$ (with initial conditions to fix $C$).

blocks.title: Method
blocks.md: 1. List $s,u,v,a,t$ with signs (choose a positive direction). 2. Choose the equation that contains the unknown and three known quantities. 3. Solve, then check the sign and units. For an object thrown up, $v=0$ at the top.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A car accelerates uniformly from 5 m/s to 20 m/s in 6 s. Find the acceleration and the distance covered.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A ball is thrown upwards at 20 m/s ($g=10$ m/s²). Find the greatest height and the total time in the air.
steps: Up is positive, $a=-10$. At the top $v=0$: $0=400-20s$, so $s=20$ m.
Time to the top: $0=20-10t$, so $t=2$ s; the fall takes the same time.

reviewNotes: Moments and equilibrium of rigid bodies are in the Upper Sixth pack.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Newton's laws
blocks.md: 1st: a particle stays at rest or moves at constant velocity unless a resultant force acts. 2nd: resultant force $F=ma$ (newtons, kg, m/s²). 3rd: every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Weight $W=mg$ (with $g=10$ m/s²).

blocks.title: Friction
blocks.md: On a rough surface friction $F\leq\mu R$ where $R$ is the normal reaction and $\mu$ the coefficient of friction. When the particle is about to slip, or is sliding, $F=\mu R$ (limiting friction). Friction opposes motion (or the tendency to move).

blocks.title: Method
blocks.md: 1. Draw a force diagram. 2. Choose the direction of motion as positive and resolve in two perpendicular directions. 3. Write $F_{net}=ma$ for each particle. For connected particles over a pulley the tension is the same on both sides and both have the same acceleration. 4. Solve. On a smooth slope of angle $\alpha$ the acceleration down the slope is $g\sin\alpha$.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Mixing mass and weight: weight is a force in N.
- On a slope the normal reaction is $mg\cos\alpha$, not $mg$.
- Writing $F=\mu R$ when the particle is not at the point of slipping (then $F<\mu R$).
- In a lift, $R\neq mg$ unless the acceleration is zero.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A 1200 kg car has an engine force of 3000 N and resistance 600 N. Find its acceleration.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A 5 kg block on a rough horizontal table ($\mu=0.4$) is pulled by a horizontal force of 30 N. Find its acceleration ($g=10$).
steps: Vertically $R=mg=50$ N, so friction $F=\mu R=0.4\times50=20$ N.
